newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar off high at the close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar off high at the close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar was marginally off its highs at the close on Tuesday as traders wound down for two days of New Year holidays on Wednesday and Thursday.
The kiwi traded higher than the US$0.7060-70 range expected by dealers earlier in the day, opening at 0.7059/66 and touching 0.7080 before closing at 0.7075/82.
On the Trade Weighted Index the kiwi firmed to 67.63 at the close after opening at 67.46.

"There is a bit of activity in the spot market, but it is pretty thin. There is some domestic corporate buying, with similar price action to yesterday but not so aggressive, from the low 0.7060s up," a Wellington-based bank dealer said.
Dealers said most analysts expected the kiwi to drift higher in offshore trading over the holiday and to rise in the short term.
"Most people expect an appreciation, but it will not take out last year's highs for some time," the dealer said.
"It is more likely to range trade with an underlying bid tone."
